prompt_en: Beside a wood fire, someone cooks banh xeo in a large cast-iron pan, next to a basket of raw herbs and a bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce.
refined_prompt: Beside a wood fire, someone cooks banh xeo in a large cast-iron pan, next to a basket of raw herbs and a bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce. In a traditional Vietnamese kitchen, a large cast-iron pan sits over a wood fire, glowing with the heat from crackling flames. A thin layer of vibrant yellow rice batter infused with turmeric sizzles and fills the air with a delightful aroma. Once set, shrimp, pork slices, and bean sprouts are carefully arranged in the center, preparing for the savory dish known as bánh xèo. Next to the pan, a basket is filled with a vibrant array of fresh herbs and vegetables, known as "rau sống," along with side dishes such as pickled vegetables and cucumber slices. A bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce is nearby, ready for dipping. The sizzle and crackle of the wood fire create a symphony of sounds that blend perfectly with the rich aroma of turmeric and fresh herbs. Friends and family eagerly anticipate the freshly made bánh xèo, which symbolizes unity and the joy of sharing a meal. "Rau sống" includes crisp lettuce, cilantro, mint, Thai basil, and cucumber slices, bringing a vibrant mix of textures and colors to the dining table. The preparation and sharing of bánh xèo, accompanied by "rau sống," is a beloved culinary tradition that captures the essence of Vietnamese culture, celebrating community and the joy found in coming together over a meal.

per_step.out_raw: ### Revised Refined Prompt Beside a wood fire, someone is carefully placing shrimp and pork slices, along with bean sprouts, onto the center of the large cast-iron pan filled with a thin layer of rice batter. The batter sizzles as it hits the hot surface, releasing a delightful aroma that quickly fills the kitchen. The batter, infused with turmeric for a vibrant yellow color, is a hallmark of Vietnamese cuisine and adds a unique flavor and golden hue to the dish. Bánh xèo, a crispy Vietnamese crepe, is deeply rooted in Vietnamese culture and is often enjoyed during celebrations and family gatherings. It is typically made with rice flour, water, and turmeric powder, creating a thin, golden batter that sizzles and crisps up as it cooks. Common fillings include shrimp, pork, and bean sprouts, all of which are added to the batter as it cooks, creating a savory and satisfying filling. Next to the pan, a basket is filled with raw herbs such as mint leaves, Thai basil, and lettuce, along with side dishes like pickled vegetables and cucumber slices. A bowl of sweet-sour fish sauce, known as nước chấm, sits nearby, ready to be used as a dipping sauce for the crispy pancakes. The aroma of freshly cooked bánh xèo, combined with the sweet scent of herbs, creates an inviting atmosphere reminiscent of a bustling market or a family kitchen. Unlike the delicate crepes of France or the fluffy pancakes of the United States, bánh xèo stands out with its crispy exterior and savory filling, embodying the essence of Vietnamese cuisine. It is not only a beloved street food in Vietnam but also a cherished dish at family gatherings, especially during festivals such as Tết (Lunar New Year). This revised prompt enhances clarity, visual detail, background, purpose, and comparable object aspects, making it an even more compelling description of bánh xèo.
